content.title: About
content.content: Baby Toddler Cookie is a soft, aromatic biscuit specially formulated for children aged 6 months to 3 years. It is made from whole grains, fruit puree, and low‑fat milk, without artificial colors, flavors, or preservatives.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cookie contains tiny pieces of dried fruit to help develop a child’s palate.
One serving (30 g) provides about 120 kcal, making it a suitable snack between meals.
The product has been safety‑tested for children as young as 12 months, including checks for small particles that could cause choking.
It is fortified with a vitamin complex (vitamins A, D, B12, folic acid).
Packaging is made from recyclable material and features a convenient resealable flap.

items.title: Supports bone growth
items.content: Added calcium and vitamin D help build strong bone tissue in growing children.

items.title: Provides steady energy
items.content: Complex carbohydrates from whole grains deliver a stable energy release without sharp blood‑sugar spikes.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and the development of a balanced gut microbiome.

items.title: Vitamin complex
items.content: B‑vitamins and vitamin A support vision, immunity, and nervous system function.

items.title: Low sugar content
items.content: Sugar is replaced with natural fruit puree, reducing the risk of cavities in toddlers.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: The cookie contains milk, so it should be avoided by children with known milk allergy.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Despite its soft texture, small pieces may pose a choking risk for infants under 6 months.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: Contains wheat; children with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should choose a gluten‑free alternative.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The cookie can be enjoyed as a standalone snack or paired with milk, yogurt, or fruit puree. For younger children, it is recommended to break the biscuit into small pieces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a tightly sealed package. After opening, consume within 2 weeks. Discard if any mold odor or discoloration appears.

content.title: About
content.content: Provolone is a semi‑hard Italian cheese made from cow’s milk, known for its mild nutty flavor and characteristic pale yellow color. It is aged from a few weeks to several months, depending on the desired intensity.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name comes from the Latin “provola,” meaning “rolled,” because the cheese is traditionally formed into a sausage‑like shape.
Provolone melts well, making it a favorite for baked dishes and golden crusts.
In Italy it is often served thinly sliced with cured meats and olives.
There are two main varieties: young (mild) and aged (sharp), distinguished by aging time.
Smoked provolone adds an extra layer of flavor.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Calcium supports bone and tooth health and plays a role in muscle function.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: Protein is essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 helps maintain the nervous system and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Provides phosphorus
items.content: Phosphorus is important for energy metabolism and dental health.

items.title: Probiotic cultures
items.content: Fermentation introduces beneficial bacteria that can support gut microbiota.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Lactose content may cause discomfort for those who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Excessive intake can contribute to elevated blood pressure.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to casein.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Provolone is calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Provolone works well in casseroles, pizza, sandwiches, and salads. Slice it thin for cold dishes, melt it in hot recipes, or serve it on a cheese board with fruit and nuts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store provolone in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C. For longer storage, wrap it in wax paper and keep it in a cold drawer. Discard if mold or off‑odors develop.

content.title: About
content.content: Fruit smoothie, bottled – a ready‑to‑drink beverage made from a blend of fresh fruits, berries and sometimes vegetables, diluted with water or juice. It is pasteurized and sealed in a hermetic glass or plastic bottle, providing a long shelf life without added preservatives.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Blends often include exotic fruits such as mango, passion fruit or kiwi, giving a more varied flavor profile.
Bottled smoothies are popular among athletes as a quick source of carbohydrates and vitamins.
Pasteurization retains most vitamins, but heat‑sensitive ones (e.g., vitamin C) can be partially degraded.
In some markets the product is sold as a “probiotic” drink, enriched with live cultures.

items.title: Rich in vitamins and antioxidants
items.content: The fruit base supplies vitamin C, vitamin A, folate and polyphenols that support immunity and protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Source of quick carbs
items.content: Naturally occurring sugars provide immediate energy, useful before workouts or during a busy day.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The high water content helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fruit fiber promotes regular bowel movements and can benefit gut microbiota.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike dairy‑based shakes, fruit smoothies typically contain negligible fat, making them suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Even though the sugars are natural, the total amount can be high, which may be unsuitable for people with diabetes or those watching their weight.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The formula may contain fruits that trigger allergies (e.g., kiwi, strawberry).

items.title: Pasteurization effect
items.content: Heat treatment can reduce the viability of added probiotic cultures.

items.title: Packaging
items.content: Plastic bottles may leach BPA over time; glass or BPA‑free containers are preferable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink straight from the bottle, chill it in the refrigerator, or add ice cubes. If desired, dilute with water or juice to lessen sweetness, and you can stir in protein powder for an extra protein boost.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bottle in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it refrigerated, tightly sealed, and consume within 3–5 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Huevos Rancheros is a classic Mexican dish consisting of fried eggs served on tortillas topped with a tomato‑chili sauce, beans, avocado, and cheese. It originated in the mid‑20th century and quickly became a popular hearty breakfast or brunch.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish is often finished with a squeeze of fresh lime for bright acidity.
Tortillas can be corn or flour, depending on regional preference.
Traditional sauce is made from fresh tomatoes, chilies, onion, and cilantro.
Huevos Rancheros is commonly served with fried potatoes or black beans on the side.
The name translates to “ranch-style eggs.”

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Eggs provide a complete source of protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Avocado and olive oil in the sauce supply monounsaturated fats that support heart health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and tomatoes deliver B6, B12, and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes and chilies are rich in lycopene and vitamin C, which help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Fiber
items.content: Black beans and tortillas add dietary fiber, aiding normal digestion.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to eggs and should avoid the dish.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Sauces and cheese can be salty; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The combination of oil, avocado, and cheese makes the dish calorie‑rich; moderation is key for weight management.

items.title: Spicy ingredients
items.content: Chili peppers may irritate the stomach of those with sensitive digestive systems.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Huevos Rancheros hot: place tortillas on a plate, layer beans, sauce, fried eggs, sliced avocado, cheese, and fresh cilantro. Finish with lime juice and accompany with salsa or guacamole.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftover tortillas in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. Keep sauce and beans refrigerated in sealed containers for up to 3 days. Use fresh eggs and vegetables promptly.

content.title: About
content.content: A peanut butter sandwich on wheat bread is a simple, satisfying snack. The combination of smooth peanut butter and soft whole‑grain bread provides a balance of protein, healthy fats, and carbohydrates.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peanut butter first appeared in the United States in the early 20th century and quickly became popular for its convenience and taste.
Whole‑grain wheat bread used in the sandwich contains more fiber than white bread, helping to keep you full longer.
The sandwich is often called an “energy bar” because it rapidly restores blood‑sugar levels.
In the U.S., more than 1.5 billion peanut butter sandwiches are sold each year.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Peanut butter provides about 25 % protein, supporting muscle repair and satiety.

items.title: Healthy monounsaturated fats
items.content: Most of the fat in peanut butter is monounsaturated, which is beneficial for cardiovascular health.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: Peanut butter is a good source of vitamin E, a powerful antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium in peanut butter supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Fiber from whole‑grain bread
items.content: The wheat bread adds dietary fiber, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Peanuts are a strong allergen; individuals with a peanut allergy may experience severe reactions.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The sandwich is calorie‑dense, so portion control is important for those watching their weight.

items.title: Sodium in bread
items.content: Some whole‑grain breads contain added salt; choose low‑sodium varieties if you need to limit sodium intake.

items.title: Aflatoxin risk
items.content: Poor‑quality peanut butter can contain aflatoxins, toxins produced by mold. Use reputable brands.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spread an even layer of peanut butter (about 2 cm) on one slice of wheat bread, top with the second slice and press gently. The sandwich can be cut into halves or quarters, and optionally topped with banana slices or a drizzle of honey.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the assembled sandwich in an airtight container at room temperature for no more than 4 hours. Store opened peanut butter in the refrigerator, and keep bread in a dry place or the fridge to prevent it from drying out.

tuna-and-rice-with-mushroom-sauce.title: Tuna and Rice with Mushroom Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Tuna and rice with mushroom sauce is a ready‑to‑eat dish containing boiled rice, chunks of tuna, and a creamy sauce made from mushrooms, cream, and spices. The meal is rich in protein, complex carbohydrates, and B‑vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tuna is one of the richest natural sources of omega‑3 fatty acids, beneficial for heart and brain health.
Mushrooms provide vitamin D and beta‑glucans that support the immune system.
Rice is traditionally used as a neutral base that lets the sauce flavor shine.
The dish can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 3 days and reheated in a microwave.
In some cuisines it is served with soy sauce or fresh herbs.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Tuna delivers about 25 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: EPA and DHA polyunsaturated fats help maintain cardiovascular health and cognitive function.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice releases glucose slowly, providing sustained energy and satiety.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tuna and rice are good sources of niacin, vitamin B6, and folate, essential for metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from mushrooms
items.content: Mushrooms contain selenium and polyphenols that combat free radicals.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: People allergic to seafood may experience reactions when consuming tuna.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The prepared sauce can be high in salt; individuals with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Improper storage may lead to growth of Salmonella or Listeria.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The combination of rice, oil in the sauce, and tuna makes the dish energy‑dense; portion control is advised for weight‑management diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, optionally garnished with fresh herbs, a squeeze of lemon, or soy sauce. It pairs well with a vegetable salad or steamed veggies.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator at +4 °C for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze portions at –18 °C and reheat before serving.
